plays.title: Personality-driven content
plays.description: Mix absurd personal wins, food milestones, and silly pop-culture edits with AI and game dev work so the feed feels human and fun.
plays.action:
1. Spot a personal stat, trip milestone, or timely event (kebabs, holidays).
2. Create a quick funny post or short video edit (e.g. exaggerated count or 'only the X' clip).
3. Frame it with 'BREAKING:' or 'To celebrate X, here's...' and keep it light.
4. Post roughly one humor piece for every three build or tool updates.

plays.title: Awesome-first curation
plays.description: Try to make things that are awesome — and publicly break down the small, delightful details in your process and tools.
plays.action:
1. Finish a small piece of a project or notice a satisfying tool behavior.
2. Capture the specific delightful detail (avoided button styles, added scanlines, a clean mechanic).
3. Post a short breakdown or screenshot thread that emphasizes why it feels awesome.
4. End with a subtle tie back to building better things.

plays.title: Share Fable 5 + Godot cross-platform prototypes
plays.description: Regularly document games built fast in Godot with Fable 5, focusing on real Android and iOS app potential.
plays.action:
1. Use Fable 5 to build or iterate a feature/level in a Godot game (fishing/pirate style or similar).
2. Record a short video clip or GIF of gameplay or the editor.
3. Tweet starting with 'Been using Fable 5 to crank out...' and call out fully baked Android (working) and iOS apps (coming soon).
4. Reply to your tweet with stack details or a link to superfun.team when it fits the project.

plays.title: Publish 'Breaking Claude News' on tool wins
plays.description: Use a consistent signature format to highlight smart AI behaviors and retro feature additions in tools like Fable and Claude.
plays.action:
1. Notice or test a specific useful capability (Fable dodging ledge-shadow buttons, classic palettes, scanlines + CRT vignette).
2. Open the post with 'Breaking Claude News:' + the win, or follow up with 'It also has...'
3. Add one sentence on why it matters to design engineers.
4. Include 1-2 screenshots and ask followers what similar small wins they've spotted.
